To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NKLR expression profile on NK cells is highly variable among donors, which can be used as a selection criterion in NK cell-based immunotherapies, as demonstrated in melanoma.
NK cells can be guided to recognize tumor cells by matching NK lysis receptor (NKLR) expression with tumor lysis ligand expression.
NKLR-guidance in the selection of donors for NK-based immunotherapy is feasible, and that NKLR-guiding can enhance the anti-tumor activity of allogeneical NK cells in HLA/KIR-mismatched settings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the feasibility of using NKLR/NKRL-ligand matching as a novel tool for augmenting NK anti-tumor activity in cell-based therapeutic approaches.
the development of a novel approach for enhancing anti-tumor activity of allogeneical NK cells.
the development of a novel NK-based immunotherapy, which is founded upon the NKLR/NK cell recognition of tumor cells, and is independent of the HLA/KIR system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NKLR/NKRL-ligand matching approach is feasible, and may be a novel and promising way to augment anti-tumor activity of allogeneically expanded NK cells.
NKLR/NKRL-ligand matching is a promising approach for improving anti tumor activity of allogeneically administered NK cells.
NK cells, which are capable of killing tumor cells, can be selected from the pool of healthy donors and expanded in culture, to be used for the treatment of patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NKLR/NK ligand matching is a novel approach for enhancing anti tumor activity of allogeneictic NK cells.
the NKLR-guided donor selection is a feasible approach for enhancing anti-tumor activity of NK cell-based therapies.
the expression profile of NKLR on NK cells can predict the ability of NK cells to kill tumor cells and that this profile can be enhanced by ex vivo expansion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
donor NK cells can be selected based on their NKLR expression profile to match the lysis-ligand profile of the tumor.
NK cell-mediated anti tumor response can be augmented by selecting donors according to the expression of NKLR, and not only by HLA/KIR matching.
the NKLR/NKRL-ligand matching is feasible, reproducible and can be applied to improve the efficacy of NK cell-based immunotherapies in the future.
